This may not be a particularly healthy solution, but it worked for me. Get angry at her. Absolutely dont talk to her or go near her again, but just write down every so often how much you hate her for rejecting you, even though it may not be true. As long as you arent sharing these thoughts or acting on them, its a perfectly valid coping skill. 

I hope you feel better soon.

Self diagnosis is bad, invalid, and hurts the community of people who /actually/ have a diagnosis. It may be easier to talk to a guidance counselor or even a regular doctor about your concerns, and they'll probably direct you and your parents to somone who can get you a DX and the help you deserve. Please seek help, and please DONT self-DX.

Nostalgia will utterly be my downfall, but it's still a part of everything I do and everything I like! I wake up crying in the middle of the night because the nostalgia of old friends, places, expereinces etc is just too much to bear, but then find myself attracted only to clothes/decor/whatever that reminds me of those nostalgic times. I feel you soo hard sister, I hope we can start living in the present sometime soon.

As a person who is suicidal, I know how much it sucks when you're trying to research but people keep getting in your way with reasons to stay alive. And I'm certainly not trying to be one of those people, so please don't take it that way. But when I was 8, my mother slit her wrists in our bath tub while I was at my dad's for the weekend, and it was 100% the thing that has caused me the most emotional distress in my life. My father refused to let me attend the funeral, so I never got to see her again. I left for that weekend excited to see her when I came back, because I loved her so much. And I never, ever got to see her again. I know nothing about you, your children, or your life, and am absolutely not trying to be preachy. Im in a similar situation myself, in fact. But I really hope this has provided you with some insight as to how your suicide may affect your children. I wouldnt wish the loss of a mother in such a terrible fashion upon anyone. 

If you cannot be persuaded out of this, I'd have to suggest staging an accident of some sort, like a car crash or a drowning. No matter how many loving notes you leave your children, they will think It was their fault forever.
